claim: The governing destination-evidence clause is weaker than the controls it supersedes: CNV-PAY-002 accepts a charity-signed bank letter alone as destination evidence, while the earlier adopted-provisional controls it overrides or leaves unreconciled required an independent callback to a separately sourced contact (UNB-RCN-GRT-017) and a 3-business-day cooling-off with notice to the previous and new channels (UNB-RCN-WF-028).
evidence: requirements/grants/END-TO-END-GRANT-LIFECYCLE-AND-OPERATING-MODEL.md:300 (UNB-RCN-GRT-017 minimum evidence combination incl. independent callback)
requirements/AUTHORITATIVE-BASELINE.md:5 (precedence: CNV clauses govern where they conflict)
requirements/discovery/2026-11-24-simplification-economics/19-REJECTED-APPROACHES.md:30 (cooling-off retained as 'primary defence against payee-redirect fraud')
why_it_matters: Forged bank letters are the standard business-email-compromise technique against grant-makers. Under the stated precedence an implementer can satisfy CNV-PAY-002 with a letter received by email and skip the callback and cooling-off. The baseline also does not say whether a destination verified for one sponsor is reused through the shared charity registry; if it is, one forged letter redirects every sponsor's payments to that charity. EDF control point: this is the single highest-leverage control against irreversible loss.
recommended_change: Amend CNV-PAY-002: destination evidence SHALL be (a) a bank-originated account-owner match, or (b) a charity document AND an independent callback to a contact sourced from the registry or a prior verified record, never from the change request. Every destination change SHALL notify the previous and new verified channels and SHALL NOT be used for release before the cooling-off period ends (default 3 business days, sponsor may lengthen, not shorten below 1). Destination records SHALL be scoped per sponsor; cross-sponsor reuse only under that sponsor's written reliance policy. AC: given only an emailed letter, release is held with DestinationEvidenceInsufficient; given a verified change on day 0, no release before day 3 and both channels received notice; given sponsor B without a reliance policy, sponsor A's verification is not reused.

perspective: software architect; regulatory perimeter; operations employee
claim: Unbound-operated blocking powers contradict the adopted regulatory perimeter, and the report says no requirement-level conflict was left unresolved. The adopted break-glass requirement lets Unbound responders freeze payments globally or per tenant and blocks payments when state changes lack a command. Unknown hold state fails closed. Platform-verified public-fact holds apply to every sponsor's grants. TVR-PAY-004 forbids any payment outside the platform gate. Against these, CNV-PAY-001 says Unbound SHALL NOT 'execute or block a payment on its own authority', and CNV-LEG-001 says Unbound SHALL NOT be able to 'indefinitely prevent a payment unilaterally'.
why_it_matters: Under the clauses as written, an Unbound outage of the hold registry (CNV-ARC-003), an Unbound freeze, or a TVR-PAY-004 gate outage can stop a sponsor from paying grants with no time limit. That is the 'unilateral prevention' CNV-LEG-001 says would trigger licensing analysis. It is also an operational single point of failure across all tenants, and it leaves unclear who is liable when a protective hold is wrong.
recommended_change: Add a ProtectiveHoldAuthority clause. Every platform-originated hold or freeze SHALL execute a hold policy that the sponsor adopted in its master agreement. It SHALL be time-bounded: it expires or converts to a sponsor decision within a sponsor-approved window, default 1 business day, and it SHALL notify sponsor treasury immediately. The sponsor SHALL always retain an out-of-platform payment path at its own bank. Any such payment SHALL be registered afterwards as OutOfBandPaymentRecorded, and duplicate detection SHALL suppress the platform instruction it matches. Amend TVR-PAY-004 to require that registration rather than forbid the payment. AC: given a platform freeze with no sponsor confirmation by the end of the window, the freeze converts to a sponsor decision task and is not silently extended. AC: given an out-of-band payment registered for grant G, the queued instruction for G is never dispatched.

claim: The required atomic hold fence at dispatch is not achievable as specified with one database per sponsor and a hold registry 'isolated by failure domain'. The research that justified fencing assumed one shared transactional core in which hold publication and release-gate visibility commit together. The only mechanism written down (registry version read 'inside the release transaction' plus a 'replicated watermark') is proposed-not-validated, and has no replication design, lag objective or failure scope.
evidence: requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:251 (CNV-ARC-001 DB per sponsor; hold registry separate schema and role, isolated by failure domain)
why_it_matters: A transaction in sponsor DB k cannot atomically read a version committed in a different database. A naive build will either check freshness, which CNV-ARC-003 forbids, or block every tenant whenever the registry or replication lags, which couples failures across tenants that are supposed to be isolated. An IRS revocation or OFAC listing must reach every sponsor cell before that cell's next dispatch.
recommended_change: Record an ADR and a clause. Global hold publications SHALL be replicated into each sponsor database as declared inter-cell contract messages with a strictly increasing version. Dispatch SHALL compare, in the same local transaction, the cell's applied version with a signed registry version beacon that is no older than a sponsor-approved maximum age. The replication lag objective (p99) SHALL be declared and benchmarked. Fail-closed scope SHALL be per cell, never global. AC (ADV-069..072 re-run per cell): a hold published at version v before dispatch prevents transmission in every cell. AC: a stalled replica in cell A blocks only cell A's dispatch. AC: a beacon older than its maximum age holds dispatch with HoldStateUnknown.

claim: Recovery objectives are undeclared, and the only concrete proposal cannot be met with the chosen topology. CNV-ARC-001 defers RTO and RPO to a benchmark. The amended refinement requires RPO 0 and 'a single consistency point across all C0 stores', but C0 now spans N sponsor databases plus the shared hold registry, the charity registry and the PII vault, each with its own point-in-time recovery. The granularity is also inconsistent: per capability in UNB-RES-003 and CNV-ARC-001, per data class in RR-UNB-RES-003-r1.
evidence: requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/data/refinements.jsonl (RR-UNB-RES-003-r1: C0 RPO 0, RTO<=4h, single consistency point)
requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:251 (CNV-ARC-001 'capability-specific RTO and RPO ... declared and benchmarked')
why_it_matters: Auditors and sponsors cannot assess continuity, and contracts cannot cite objectives. RPO 0 is realistic on managed PostgreSQL only with synchronous in-region replication. Across regions, or across independently restored databases, it needs explicitly approved recovery semantics. Without them a restore can resurrect a payment intent whose hold was published after the restore point.
recommended_change: Replace with one versioned table keyed by data class and isolation profile. C0 SHALL have RPO 0 within region through synchronous standby. Cross-region recovery SHALL have a declared nonzero RPO under the approved recovery semantics CNV-ARC-001 allows. Consistency SHALL be per sponsor cell, plus a cross-store reconciliation procedure: re-apply holds published after the restore point, verify PII-vault references, and reconcile with providers before release unblocks. AC: restore tenant T to time t, replay hold publications after t, and confirm payment release stays blocked until reconciliation passes. AC: the annual drill shows achieved RPO and RTO per class.

claim: Operational complexity has moved, not gone away. Excluding Kubernetes and Terraform while making a separate managed database per sponsor the default produces a database fleet (an E5 administrator means 50 or more HA instances). Each needs migrations in lockstep with one codebase ('both cells report the same release version before traffic resumes'), its own outbox and scheduler, per-tenant keys and backups, and PostgreSQL major-version upgrades. Strata supports PostgreSQL 16 only, and retention runs 10 years. No requirement covers fleet provisioning, partial migration failure or the per-tenant cost floor.
evidence: requirements/reconciliation/2026-11-23/data/refinements.jsonl (RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 Profile B default; AC-4 same release before traffic resumes)
requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/07-ECHELON-CAPABILITY-ASSESSMENT.md §4 (Strata PG16 only) and gap table STRATA-GAP-02
why_it_matters: A failed migration on one of 50 databases either blocks every tenant's release or leaves the fleet on mixed versions, which the identical-release rule forbids. Small sponsors (E2, about 1,500 funds) pay an HA-instance floor they do not need. Without declarative provisioning, the work lands in manual console steps that cannot be audited as ITGC change management.
recommended_change: Add requirements. Fleet provisioning SHALL be declarative and version-controlled, using any tool including provider-native templates, under ITGC change control. Schema changes SHALL be expand/contract, so release N runs against schema N-1 and N, with migration state recorded per tenant. A failed tenant migration SHALL leave that tenant on the compatible prior schema without blocking others. The default isolation profile SHALL be chosen only after the ADR-009 cost benchmark at 10, 100 and 1,000 tenants. A PostgreSQL major-version upgrade drill SHALL run before acceptance. AC: a migration failure on 1 of 50 cells leaves the other 49 upgraded and the failed cell serving on N-1, with the incident recorded.

claim: The E5 outsourced-administrator operating model has no tenancy or authority construct. The administrator pools service and operations staff across 50 sponsors, but the tenant is the legal sponsor, the entity model (Tenant, LegalSponsor, DistributionPartner, Program, Fund, DeploymentCell) has no administrator or service-organization principal, and the case kernel assumes sponsor-scoped queues.
why_it_matters: Pooled agents either need a cross-tenant work view, which is a cross-tenant read model the isolation rules do not cover, or must hop between 50 sessions, which defeats the economics of report 05. Implementers will improvise a cross-database queue holding donor PII.
recommended_change: Add an Administrator principal type that holds a per-sponsor ServiceDelegation (task classes, data classes, expiry) recorded in each sponsor's cell. A federated queue projection SHALL contain only routing metadata (case id, kind, priority, due time, sponsor id) and no donor PII. Opening an item SHALL bind a VerifiedTenantContext for that sponsor. Administrator staff SHALL be limited to non-reserved command classes. AC: an administrator agent sees items from 3 sponsors in one queue, but opening an item for sponsor B without B's delegation returns RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND and logs a denial. AC: the queue projection contains no field classified as personal data.

claim: CNV-GOV-004 forbids any person from holding reserved authority for more than one sponsor. That conflicts with its own allowance for contracted and fractional holders, with independent reconsideration reviewers (CNV-GRT-012), with pre-contracted December surge reviewers (CNV-SVC-002) and with the decision-team floors the model accepts for E2 and E5 (TEV-003). Its acceptance criterion also needs cross-tenant identity correlation that no isolation requirement specifies.
why_it_matters: The market for qualified contracted reviewers (fractional CFOs, outside counsel, compliance consultants) is made up of people who serve several organizations. Banning them makes small-sponsor staffing and the December surge plan infeasible. Enforcing the ban needs a global person registry that crosses tenant boundaries.
recommended_change: Replace the absolute ban with a conflict rule. A person MAY hold reserved authority for several sponsors only if each sponsor's board resolution records the other appointments, the person attests that they have no relationship to any fund, donor or recipient in the matter, and the person never decides a matter that involves two of their sponsors (for example a sponsor-to-sponsor transfer). Cross-sponsor checks SHALL use a privacy-preserving identity token in the shared party core, not shared PII. AC: an appointment with undisclosed other appointments is rejected. AC: a transfer from sponsor A to sponsor B cannot be decided by a person appointed by both.

claim: Authority vocabularies are inconsistent across normative text still in force, and the single authority matrix that was meant to reconcile them (UNB-RCN-PLT-005) was never converged. The tiers in force: A0-A5, where A3 is 'controlled consequential action' and A4 is reserved; CNV-GOV-004's 'Reserved (A3+)'; CNV-AIO-001's recommend, prepare and execute, with execute available to agents; UNB-AGT-002's 'agents SHALL NOT ... write authoritative records'; REQ-X-017's Tier 2 = AI; CNV-GRT-011's Tier 2 = enhanced human review; and PA-1..4 in CNV-GOV-003's acceptance criterion.
evidence: requirements/ai/AI-NATIVE-INTERACTION-AND-AGENT-COLLABORATION.md:106 (CNV-AIO-001 'permitted agent level: recommend, prepare or execute')
why_it_matters: Whether an agent may execute anything, and whether preparing a payment instruction needs a board-appointed officer, depends on which vocabulary an implementer reads. One reading adds unnecessary human approvals; the other lets agents write authoritative records. Auditors cannot map authority to controls.
recommended_change: Converge UNB-RCN-PLT-005 into a normative AuthorityMatrix (command class x actor type {deterministic policy, AI agent, staff role, appointed officer, board} x level). CNV-AIO-001 SHALL enumerate the agent-executable command set; for release 1 it SHALL contain only A2 reversible internal actions. Rename CNV-GRT-011's tier to 'Enhanced review'. CNV-GOV-004 SHALL reference A4. AC: CI fails if any requirement, command or UI references a level not in the matrix. AC: an agent invoking a command outside its executable set is rejected with AuthorityRequired.

perspective: security attacker (AI prompt injection); customer service employee
claim: Prompt-injection controls cover tool calls but not the main channel through which AI affects money: AI-prepared dossiers that humans approve in batches. Without a board delegation, the operating model is 'individual accountable batch decisions on AI-prepared dossiers'. Charity websites and documents can carry injected text that biases the narrative or drops a deterministic flag, and nothing requires deterministic findings to be rendered independently of the AI narrative. The path when AI is unavailable is also undefined (the November scenario has inference down for 2 days).
why_it_matters: A batch approver who trusts the summary carries out the attacker's intent without any tool call, so the existing controls never fire. When AI is down, sponsors without a delegation lose their dossier pipeline in peak season.
recommended_change: Add a DecisionDossier requirement. Deterministic findings (eligibility, sanctions, holds, related-party, Tier-2 triggers) SHALL render in a separate section built from sources and hashes, which the AI can neither edit nor reorder. AI narrative SHALL be labelled and SHALL quote untrusted sources only as quoted, attributed text. A batch approval SHALL require item-level confirmation for every item that carries a deterministic flag. A deterministic-only dossier SHALL be produced when AI is unavailable. AC: a charity PDF containing 'ignore the revocation' still shows the revocation flag first, and the approver cannot batch-approve that item. AC: with AI disabled, every dossier still renders its deterministic section.

claim: The 'single authoritative entry point' cannot itself be relied on. baseline.jsonl truncates statement text to 300 characters with no content hash (535 of 1,619 rows end exactly at the 300-character cap). It reports 97 reconciliation records as 'recorded' although their domain files mark them adopted-provisional, because the generator reads approval_status or validation_status fields those records lack. And no clause row shows whether it rests on an owner-approved direction or one of the 113 agent-recommended answers still awaiting ratification.
why_it_matters: Reviewers who read the index as instructed will treat binding payee-fraud and accessibility controls as non-normative, and cannot see which clauses are provisional. Truncated text without a hash breaks traceability for any requirement-to-control or IPE evidence.
recommended_change: Each baseline row SHALL carry full text or a SHA-256 of the exact source text plus file and line. Status SHALL be derived from the domain-file adoption marker. Each CNV row SHALL carry approval_basis {owner-approved, agent-recommended-pending-ratification} and the resolving question ids. AC: the validator fails when any row's text hash differs from its source or when the row status differs from its domain-file adoption marker.

claim: The control register is not linked to the converged baseline and does not record who operates each control. No governance CSV references any CNV clause. The master matrix has a single generic 'owner_role_proposed' column (for example 'Governance Lead') with no split between service-organization controls, complementary user-entity controls (CUECs) and subservice controls, even though CNV-GOV-001 requires CUEC mapping and most key financial controls (approval, reconciliation, OFAC dispositions, NAV approval) are run by the sponsor.
evidence: requirements/governance/MASTER-ENTERPRISE-CONTROL-MATRIX.csv header and rows (owner_role_proposed; status Designed; test_executed No)
why_it_matters: Neither Unbound's service auditor nor a sponsor's financial-statement auditor can scope reliance, because Unbound's SOC 1 would cover ITGCs and automated controls while the sponsor performs the judgmental ones. Evidence cannot be produced for controls whose operator is undefined.
recommended_change: Extend the authoritative register with: control_operator {Unbound, sponsor, administrator, rail partner, custodian}; report_relevance {SOC1, SOC2, none}; cuec_id; automated or manual; and the evidence query (IPE definition). Every CNV clause classified as an internal control SHALL map to at least one control row. AC: the validator fails when a control-class CNV clause has no mapping or a mapped control has no operator. AC: the generated management description lists CUECs per sponsor.

claim: CNV-GOV-001 contradicts itself. It says 'no sponsor-count trigger ... SHALL be required' and then requires a SOC 1 type 2 to be planned once 'two or more user entities exist'. Its activation gate (a recorded external-auditor planned approach before production reliance) may also be impossible for first-year sponsors whose auditors set their approach after onboarding.
why_it_matters: An implementer cannot tell when a report is required, and the gate may block onboarding until audit season.
recommended_change: Choose one trigger. A SOC 1 type 2 SHALL be planned when any user auditor states an intent to rely; the 2-entity trigger SHALL either be removed or relabelled as a business-policy default with an owner. Production MAY activate with a recorded 'planned approach pending' together with the sponsor CFO's acceptance of substantive-testing support (evidence pack plus right to audit). AC: a sponsor with no auditor approach but a recorded CFO acceptance can activate, and the evidence pack is generated monthly.

claim: After a sponsor exits, the exit rules delete Unbound's own service-organization evidence along with tenant data: a read-only copy for 90 days after export confirmation, then backups within 35 days. That evidence (operator-access records, change records, IPE run logs, TPSP audit-cooperation records) must survive for the SOC examination period and for later claims, such as ACH warranty claims of up to two years.
evidence: requirements/FULL-ACCOUNTING-SYSTEM.md:326 (CNV-FIN-003 warranty claims up to two years)
why_it_matters: Unbound would be unable to support its own SOC report, an ODFI audit or a dispute about processing it performed before the exit.
recommended_change: Add a retention class 'service-organization evidence' that Unbound owns, separate from tenant records. It SHALL hold only the minimum tenant identifiers and be kept for at least the longest of the SOC period plus 3 years, the Nacha audit horizon, or the contractual period. It SHALL be listed on the exit certificate. AC: after exit and deletion, operator-access and change evidence for the exited tenant's last SOC period can still be retrieved, and contains no donor PII.

claim: Reconciliation activation is circular. CNV-FIN-004 refuses activation of any tolerance configuration without calibration evidence 'from actual feeds', yet feeds exist only after activation. The same pattern recurs in CNV-SVC-002 (thresholds calibrated in a pilot) and CNV-EVB-001.
why_it_matters: Read literally, no sponsor can ever activate reconciliation. Read loosely, implementers will ship uncalibrated tolerances, which the clause was written to prevent.
recommended_change: Define a ProvisionalCalibration state. Tolerances SHALL be zero (exact match only), every non-exact item SHALL go to the human queue, and the sample rate SHALL be 100% of non-exact items for at least one full close cycle of parallel run. After that, the controller SHALL approve tolerances from the observed distribution. AC: during the provisional state no item auto-passes on tolerance. AC: activating non-zero tolerance without observed-distribution evidence is refused.

claim: CNV-FIN-004 withholds statements 'only for affected funds' but gives no rule for breaks that cannot be attributed to a fund, which is the common case at bank-account level in pooled disbursement or operating accounts. Withholding a statement can also breach program terms, which CNV-PLT-005 says override defaults.
evidence: requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:243 (CNV-PLT-005 'any cadence promised in program terms SHALL override defaults')
why_it_matters: Faced with an unattributable break, operations will either withhold every statement or publish every one, and both choices conflict with a clause. Customer service gets donors asking for statements that were contractually promised.
recommended_change: Add: a break SHALL be attributed to funds through its unmatched items. An unattributable break SHALL open a controller decision due within N business days (sponsor-set), choosing between publishing all affected statements with a 'provisional - reconciliation pending' marker and withholding them with donor notice. Program-terms templates SHALL reserve the right to delay for reconciliation. AC: an unattributable $500 break on a pooled account opens the controller decision and does not silently withhold statements.

claim: CNV-FIN-007 makes ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee the default recognition point, with the 'notice sent atomically with approval'. An external notice cannot be atomic with a database commit; the outbox records only the intent to send. The acceptance criterion (approval on 31 December, expense posts in December) leaves undefined what happens when delivery is on 1 January, fails, or goes to an anonymous-donor grant.
evidence: research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/COMPONENT-MONOLITH-EVENT-ORDERING-AND-CONSISTENCY-2026-11-23.md 'Outbox' ('Never assume database transaction and external ... one atomic operation')
why_it_matters: Year-end cutoff, which drives grant expense and payable, will be tested by auditors against evidence of communication. A definition that cannot be evidenced fails that test.
recommended_change: Define 'communicated' as: a notice made available to the grantee through a durable channel (portal posting, or recorded delivery to the grantee's verified address) at a timestamp. Recognition SHALL use that timestamp, and the cutoff register SHALL list approved-but-undelivered notices. AC: an approval at 23:59 on 31 December with portal posting at 23:59 is recognized in December. AC: email bounced and no portal posting means the grant is listed as approved-uncommunicated at year end.

claim: An owner-directed binding scope still in force contradicts CNV-FIN-012. FULL-ACCOUNTING-SYSTEM.md requires 'a complete integrated accounting system, not just ... external GL connector', including AP, AR, purchasing, payroll interface and fixed assets. CNV-FIN-012 makes those ERP integrations by default and allows a shadow book only on demonstrated demand, but its amends list covers only refinement records, and the binding-scope paragraph and UNB-ACC-004/012/013 are not annotated.
why_it_matters: Scope can swing by a whole ERP depending on which text the reader treats as governing. Effort estimates and the book-of-record map diverge.
recommended_change: Add the binding-scope paragraph and UNB-ACC-004/012/013 to CNV-FIN-012's amends list, annotate them as 'available on demand, not release-1', and record the owner's ratification. AC: the baseline validator flags any unannotated original whose subject overlaps a CNV clause's function map.

claim: Mandatory Strata requirements still in force contradict verified capability and the converged architecture. UNB-TEC-STRATA-001..004 make Strata a 'binding product selection' for authoritative event persistence, says 'database engine not yet selected', and treat any limitation as a blocker. Report 07 verifies Strata v0.1.1 as a PostgreSQL-16-only DDL pilot with no append-only or temporal capability, and the reconciliation refinement that confines Strata to schema management is only proposed-not-validated.
why_it_matters: Read literally, the baseline blocks implementation, because a mandated component cannot do what it is mandated for. Teams may also bend the ledger design to fit a pilot tool.
recommended_change: Add a clause superseding UNB-TEC-STRATA-001..004. Strata SHALL be used for declarative schema governance where its supported PostgreSQL versions match production. Authoritative append-only history SHALL be an Unbound-owned ledger component on managed PostgreSQL. Strata version support SHALL be a precondition of each PostgreSQL major upgrade, otherwise Strata SHALL be bypassed for that cell. AC: the architecture acceptance checklist has no requirement that depends on unverified Strata capability.

claim: The definition of the tenant unit is contradictory. CNV-ARC-002 makes the legal sponsor the tenant. UNB-TEN-001..008, still in force, give 'every partner' an immutable tenant identity and partner-level isolation profiles, including a dedicated database and infrastructure per partner. The architecture says 'Partner tenant is not necessarily the sponsor'.
why_it_matters: If a distribution partner contractually demands dedicated infrastructure while its sponsor also serves other partners, the sponsor's books and atomic capacity reservations split across cells. That breaks CNV-FIN-012 and CNV-FIN-001, and leaves the isolation tests aimed at the wrong boundary.
recommended_change: Amend UNB-TEN-001..008: isolation profiles SHALL be selected per legal sponsor. Partner and program isolation SHALL be enforced inside the sponsor cell by typed partitioning and negative tests. A partner that requires dedicated infrastructure SHALL be served by a dedicated sponsor cell, or by a separate sponsor entity. AC: provisioning a partner-level dedicated cell for a sponsor that already has a cell is rejected. AC: a partner P1 principal querying P2 data in the same sponsor cell receives zero rows.

claim: The default grant payment rail is stated two ways. CNV-PAY-001 says release-1 grant payments 'SHALL use networked rail partners acting as the sponsor's agent, with sponsor-originated ACH as fallback'. CNV-GRT-016 says 'Verified ACH SHALL be the default rail', and report 04 says ACH by default through the sponsor's ODFI or a partner.
why_it_matters: The rail choice determines who verifies destinations (partner or sponsor), which debit blocks are needed (CNV-PAY-007), who holds Nacha obligations and how return files are matched. Building both as defaults doubles integration and test scope.
recommended_change: State one rule: the rail SHALL be selected per program in the CNV-PAY-001 role table. The release-1 default SHALL be [owner decision], and the alternative SHALL be the fallback, sharing one PaymentInstruction contract. For each rail, specify who verifies destinations and who handles returns. AC: a program without a selected primary rail cannot activate payments. AC: fallback dispatch for a grant reuses the original idempotency chain.

claim: The baseline does not say whether a Notification of Change (NOC) counts as a 'bank-detail change'. CNV-PAY-002 requires NOCs to be applied within six banking days 'under change control', requires new destination evidence 'after any bank-detail change', and CNV-GOV-005 requires independent approval for material changes. UNB-RCN-WF-028 adds a 3-day cooling-off and dual-channel notice.
why_it_matters: If an NOC counts as a change, cooling-off, evidence collection and independent approval can push it past the Nacha deadline. If it does not, the rule must say why bank-originated data is trusted, so that charity-initiated changes cannot be dressed up as NOCs.
recommended_change: Classify a bank-originated NOC, matched on original trace, change code and COR trace, as an evidence class that satisfies destination evidence without cooling-off. It SHALL notify the charity's verified channels and SHALL be logged under change control, without a separate human approval. Any charity-initiated change stays under the full control. AC: an NOC received on day 0 is applied before the next entry or by day 6 with no human approval. AC: a charity-submitted change that cites an NOC still goes through cooling-off.

claim: Failure behaviour when a bank feed goes stale is incomplete. CNV-PAY-007 fails 'new releases' closed once staleness exceeds the approved window, but it does not carry TEV-004's alternative path (already-reserved approvals may proceed when the bank confirms collected funds through another verified channel). It also does not define 'new release', or say who approves the window and its maximum.
why_it_matters: A three-day feed outage in December would stop all grant payments for the affected sponsors with no sanctioned way to continue, which pushes treasury staff to pay through the bank portal outside the platform.
recommended_change: Add: when the feed is stale, releases of grants already reserved MAY proceed on an AlternativeBalanceAttestation (a bank portal balance captured and attested by two treasury staff, valid for 1 business day), capped at the attested collected balance less outstanding instructions. New reservations SHALL still fail closed. The sponsor treasurer SHALL approve the staleness window, with a ceiling of 2 business days. AC: with the feed 30 hours stale and an attestation recorded, reserved grants release up to the attested amount and new approvals are held with StaleBankFeed.

claim: The insider path through engineering and infrastructure is not covered. CNV-ARC-002 governs operator access to data, and CNV-GOV-003 stops sponsor approvers from deploying the gate. But Unbound engineers who change the deterministic gate's code, run schema migrations, or hold managed-PostgreSQL admin roles affect every sponsor at once. No baseline row requires two-person code review of control-relevant modules, signed or reproducible builds, sponsor-visible change notices for gate logic, or externally anchored tamper evidence; the architecture's 'checkpoint digests stored independently' was never adopted as a requirement.
evidence: requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl (no rows matching code review / reproducible build / anchor)
why_it_matters: A single engineer could weaken an eligibility or sanctions rule across all tenants, and the change would look like ordinary releases. The sponsor's auditor relies on Unbound's ITGCs for exactly this risk.
recommended_change: Add requirements. Modules tagged control-relevant (gate, ledger, reservations, holds, authority, dispatch) SHALL require two approvers on every change, neither of them the author. Builds SHALL be signed with recorded provenance. Every release SHALL publish a per-sponsor notice listing changed control-relevant behaviour. Ledger checkpoint digests SHALL be anchored outside Unbound's administrative boundary, daily. Production DB admin roles SHALL be break-glass only. AC: merging a gate change with one approval is blocked. AC: altering a posted journal row through a DB superuser is detected at the next checkpoint verification and blocks affected payments.

claim: Shared cross-tenant stores have multiplied without a normative data-class inventory: the 'minimal shared party core' (CNV-ARC-002), the charity registry and neutral flags (CNV-GRT-004), cross-sponsor disposition reuse (CNV-GRT-006), cross-sponsor person checks (CNV-GOV-004), cross-sponsor shadow evaluation (CNV-GOV-005), benchmarks (CNV-ECO-001), and shared models and evaluation datasets (UNB-TEN-009). The only isolation acceptance criteria test operator queries.
why_it_matters: Each shared store is a channel for cross-tenant inference or leakage. One example: a neutral flag visible only to sponsors with pending grants reveals that another sponsor is investigating. Database-per-sponsor gives a false sense of isolation while these shared stores remain uncatalogued.
recommended_change: Publish a normative SharedStoreRegister listing each cross-tenant store, its permitted fields and their classification, its writers and readers, and the inference risks it carries. Donor and advisor PII SHALL NOT enter any shared store except as a keyed token for authorized checks. Each store SHALL have differential isolation tests. AC: for each shared API, a tenant-B request returns no value derived from tenant-A private data (fuzzed). AC: adding a field without a register entry fails CI.

claim: No converged clause controls changes to donor or advisor contact channels or successor designations. CNV-PLT-003 covers identity proofing and refuses bank-detail changes below CAL3, but changing email, phone or address, or successor and beneficiary designations, has no notice to the previous channel and no cooling-off before high-risk actions. Report 04's September credential-stuffing scenario relies only on 'risk-based step-up'.
evidence: requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl (only AUTH-I7 and UNB-RCN-WF-028 mention cooling-off; WF-028 covers charity destinations only)
why_it_matters: Takeover attacks normally start by changing the contact channel so the real owner stops receiving alerts. After that the attacker can redirect successor designations or route grants to a colluding charity.
recommended_change: Add: a change to any verified contact channel SHALL notify the previous channel with a self-service revert link. For a sponsor-set period (default 72 hours) after the change, successor and beneficiary changes, authority changes and grant recommendations above a sponsor threshold SHALL be held for confirmation through the previous channel or step-up. AC: email changed and a successor change submitted 1 hour later leaves the successor change pending and sends notice to the old email.

claim: Assurance rules leave some donors with no workable path to essential changes. Bank-detail changes need CAL3, which is mapped only to an achieved AAL. Account-summary disclosure needs a possession factor or an authenticated portal handoff. Step-up proofing uses documents plus a selfie or live video. Nothing provides an accessible alternative for blind, deaf or phone-only donors, and the baseline mentions no TTY or relay service.
why_it_matters: Older and disabled donors are a large DAF population. CNV-GOV-006 makes accessibility non-removable, but without a concrete path service staff must either refuse the request or bypass the control.
recommended_change: Add an AccessibleAssurancePath requirement covering at least: a one-time code mailed to the verified address, an outbound call to a verified number, assisted video with captioning, and in-person or notarized verification. Each reaches a defined CAL level. Relay calls (TRS) SHALL be accepted and SHALL NOT be treated as elevated risk on that basis alone. AC: a blind donor without a smartphone completes a bank-detail change through mailed code plus outbound call within 10 business days. AC: a relay call reaches the same CAL as a direct call with the same factors.

claim: The WCAG 2.2 AA mandate is not backed by testable acceptance or capable dependencies. CNV-EXP-001's only acceptance criterion is a brand-contrast compile failure. Forma has about 40 known accessibility issues, Chromium-only evidence and no conformance statement. Folio claims no tagged PDF or PDF/UA. Accessible-at-issuance (UNB-RCN-PLT-010) shows as 'recorded' in the baseline. Nothing covers adjustable timing against reauthentication timeouts (WCAG 2.2.1), alternate formats (large print or braille) for statements and acknowledgments, or issuance when the PDF pipeline fails.
why_it_matters: Acknowledgments are legally time-sensitive, because donors need contemporaneous written acknowledgment. If statement publication is gated on accessibility verification while the PDF pipeline is still unbuilt, the gate can delay legal documents.
recommended_change: Add acceptance criteria. Each surface SHALL publish an Accessibility Conformance Report from automated tests plus manual assistive-technology testing before activation. Every issued document SHALL be available as accessible HTML from the same snapshot at issuance; PDFs SHALL pass PDF/UA-1 (veraPDF) or be marked supplementary. If the PDF pipeline fails, issuance SHALL proceed with HTML and the integrity hash, and SHALL NOT be withheld. Sessions SHALL warn before timeout and allow extension. Alternate formats SHALL be provided within a sponsor-set number of business days. AC: with the PDF renderer down at year end, acknowledgments still issue as accessible HTML on time.

claim: Behaviour will be hard to explain to donors and charities. Payments carry seven orthogonal state dimensions; contributions carry four dates; declines use a neutral catalog. No normative mapping exists from internal state to donor-, charity- and staff-facing labels, and nothing defines what a service agent may see or say about compliance holds.
evidence: research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PRECISE-PAYMENT-STATE-MACHINE-AND-RAIL-PROOF-CONTRACT-2026-11-23.md 'Separate orthogonal state dimensions' ('A UI may derive a concise label')
why_it_matters: Inconsistent labels create calls and complaints, and every complaint triggers CNV-PLT-005 clocks. Agents who see raw OFAC detail risk disclosing it; agents who see nothing cannot help.
recommended_change: Add a normative StatusProjection table that maps every reachable combination of the payment, grant and contribution dimensions to a donor label, a charity label, a staff label, an approved explanation script and the next expected event or date. Add a staff disclosure matrix by role, for example service agents see 'compliance review' and the due date, and only the compliance role sees list details. AC: a generated test confirms every reachable state combination maps to exactly one label per audience. AC: moderated usability tests with donors reach a sponsor-set comprehension threshold before activation.

claim: Configurable policies can conflict, and nothing detects it. Examples: the CNV-GRT-015 hold-or-warn option against the CNV-GRT-003 fail-safe; CNV-ENT-001 'approved unpaid grants proceed unless sponsor policy says otherwise' against CNV-GRT-016 joint authority and the CNV-ENT-002 dispute freeze; CNV-PLT-005 contractual cadence against CNV-FIN-004 withholding; and a kill switch that disables intake while hold release depends on the same flag (XFC-SAS-003). CNV-GOV-005 requires shadow replay but no logical conflict analysis, and the REQ-X-018 precedence order is still 'Proposed'.
why_it_matters: Shadow replay finds only conflicts that occur in the replayed sample. Rare combinations such as a dispute plus a death plus a recurring grant reach production undetected.
recommended_change: Adopt a normative precedence lattice: law > platform non-removable > sponsor board policy > program terms > fund agreement > donor preference. At adoption time, require static analysis of a policy pack against the lattice and the other active packs, rejecting rules that overlap with different outcomes unless an explicit priority is recorded. AC: a pack that lets approved grants proceed after death, adopted alongside an active dispute freeze on the same fund, is rejected with PolicyConflict and names both rules.

claim: Cumulative delegation-of-authority (DoA) aggregation in CNV-GOV-007 ('by entity, beneficiary or counterparty ... across approvers within a 30-day window') will generate unnecessary human approvals in a DAF program. Thousands of unrelated donors grant to the same large charities, and the acceptance criterion aggregates two $9,000 approvals 'to the same counterparty'.
why_it_matters: At E1 or E4 volume in December, every popular recipient would trip escalation. That consumes the reviewer capacity TEV-001 already shows is short, and trains approvers to rubber-stamp.
recommended_change: Scope aggregation to transactions that share a fund, a related-party group (donor household or 35% entities), the requesting principal, or a sponsor-operating payable counterparty. Recipient-level aggregation across unrelated funds SHALL be a detective analytic, not an approval gate. AC: two $9,000 grants from unrelated funds to the same charity do not aggregate. AC: two $9,000 grants from the same donor's two funds to one charity do. AC: false-positive rate is measured in shadow replay before activation.

claim: Several AI clauses cannot be tested as written, or create a large unverified instruction surface. CNV-AIO-001 requires assistance metadata on every API operation, configuration field, input and template, including 'financial and regulatory implications', but the only acceptance criterion checks that the metadata exists. CNV-LEG-001 expects an 'AI feature proposing a donor-specific allocation change' to be refused with AdviceNotPermitted, which no free-text classifier can guarantee deterministically.
why_it_matters: Thousands of hand-written regulatory-implication notes will drift out of date and be fed to agents as trusted context. A probabilistic refusal presented as a deterministic control will fail an audit test.
recommended_change: Generate assistance metadata from typed schemas and validation rules wherever possible. Text on regulatory implications SHALL have an owner, a version and an effective date, and SHALL be sampled for review each release. Metadata SHALL be loaded only from the signed build. Restate CNV-LEG-001: no AI tool or output schema SHALL be able to express a fund-specific security or allocation instruction, with output filtering added as defence in depth. AC: the AI tool registry contains no tool whose schema includes security, allocation or weight fields for a fund. AC: a review sample of 5% of regulated-implication entries has zero unowned entries.

claim: All 63 convergence clauses list empty dependencies, although real ones exist. CNV-GRT-006 dispatch fencing depends on CNV-ARC-003, CNV-GOV-003 on CNV-GOV-004, CNV-FIN-012 capacity on CNV-FIN-001, CNV-PAY-002 on the CNV-PAY-001 role table, and CNV-GRT-001 on CNV-GOV-005 versioning. 44 clauses carry external activation gates (board resolutions, auditor letters, bank and acquirer agreements, registrations), but there is no per-operating-model activation plan or minimum viable activation set.
why_it_matters: Build order and sponsor onboarding cannot be planned, partial activation can enable a clause before what it relies on, and sponsors face an unbounded list of documents to produce. This is the onboarding-friction counterpart of 'complexity moved to the customer'.
recommended_change: Fill in dependencies for every clause and validate that the graph has no cycles. Generate an activation plan per operating model (E1 to E5) listing each gate's artefact, owner and template. Define a minimum activation profile for a first sponsor. AC: the validator fails on a cycle or on a clause that references another clause's mechanism without declaring the dependency. AC: CNV-GOV-005 activation refuses any element whose dependency is inactive.

claim: Nothing defines how long-running workflow instances behave when their definition changes. Process managers are 'versioned rows', but successor windows (90 to 365 days), reconsideration windows, discretionary holds of up to 180 days, recurring series and dormancy timers span many releases, and no clause says whether an in-flight instance stays on its original definition or is migrated.
why_it_matters: This is the main hidden complexity of in-database orchestration. Without a rule, a release can silently change deadlines or steps for open cases, including statutory ones, and auditors cannot reconstruct which rules governed a case.
recommended_change: Add: every process instance SHALL record the definition version and policy version it started under. A new definition SHALL apply only to new instances unless an explicit, tested migration function is released, which SHALL record a MigrationApplied fact per instance and SHALL never shorten a statutory or notified deadline. AC: after deploying definition v2, open v1 successor cases keep their notified deadlines, and a migration to v2 is recorded per instance.

claim: The Echelon dependencies do not yet support the mandated ownership model. CNV-EXP-001 says reusable application-layer components 'SHALL be owned by Forma'. Report 07 finds Forma's registry channel behind its release (1.0.1 against 1.1.0), no money input or app shell, the Limen protocol still at 0.x and liable to change in minor releases, no IdP, Folio without a renderer, and PolyForm Noncommercial terms across most of the stack. CNV-GOV-007 requires a commercial licence only 'before commercial launch'.
why_it_matters: Critical-path fixes (money input, accessibility issues, app shell) depend on an external upstream with no service level. A paid pilot with sponsors is arguably already commercial use under a noncommercial licence. Ownership is unclear when upstream does not deliver.
recommended_change: Amend CNV-EXP-001: Forma is the preferred owner, but an Unbound adapter MAY remain indefinitely when the upstream service level is not met. Each adopted Echelon component SHALL be pinned by release-manifest digest and covered by Unbound contract tests. The commercial licence, or a written pilot-use grant, SHALL be in place before the implementation gate and before any sponsor pilot that involves payment. AC: the build fails if a component is pinned to an untagged commit. AC: the implementation-gate checklist requires a licence artefact.

claim: Under a WebAssembly-first client there is no requirement that authorization, policy evaluation and capacity computation run on the server. Report 07 notes that Limen guards are 'not an authorization boundary', and the baseline has no row on server-side authority, so F# domain logic shared with the browser could be trusted from the client.
evidence: requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/07-ECHELON-CAPABILITY-ASSESSMENT.md §1 Routing ('Guards are explicitly not an authorization boundary')
why_it_matters: A modified client could submit pre-evaluated 'policy passed' results or capacity figures. Shared F# code makes that mistake easy to make.
recommended_change: Add: every authorization decision, policy evaluation, eligibility gate, capacity or fee computation and state transition SHALL be computed or re-verified on the server inside the command transaction. Client-side results SHALL be advisory display only, and API contracts SHALL NOT accept client-computed decision fields. AC: a tampered WASM client that sends policyResult=Pass for a failing grant is rejected, and the event is logged.

claim: The monolith design does not isolate workloads. Statement runs (quarterly, for up to 500,000 funds in E4), PDF rendering, AI work, reporting and benchmark queries share the process and databases with reservation and dispatch. CNV-ARC-001 sets no workload-isolation requirement, although the research flags ADV-075 (a reporting query starving payments).
why_it_matters: The modular monolith is appropriate for this domain, because atomic approval plus reservation and the fencing invariants favour one transactional core. That case holds only if peak batch work cannot starve the critical path, and December concentrates both.
recommended_change: Add: critical command paths (reservation, release, dispatch, hold publication) SHALL have reserved connection pools and worker capacity. Batch, reporting and AI work SHALL read from replicas or snapshots under statement timeouts and run in separately scaled worker roles of the same build. The benchmark SHALL include a December peak running alongside a statement run. AC: during a full statement run, p99 reservation latency stays within its declared SLO.

claim: Failure of a rail partner is unhandled. Release 1 routes grant payments through networked rail partners acting as the sponsor's agent, who may hold sponsor funds in transit. Nothing covers partner outage, insolvency, funds-in-transit exposure limits, or switching to the fallback rail without duplicate payments. CNV-GOV-002 covers only SOC-report gaps.
evidence: requirements/DEFERRED-PAYMENTS-AND-REMAINING-GAPS.md:176 (CNV-PAY-007 debit blocks allow rail partners funding by ACH debit)
why_it_matters: Funds pulled by a partner through ACH debit but not yet disbursed are a concentrated loss exposure. A naive switch to the sponsor's own ACH during a partner outage can double-pay grants the partner later executes.
recommended_change: Add a RailPartnerResilience requirement. The sponsor SHALL approve a maximum funds-in-transit exposure per partner, enforced on debit-funding requests. A partner outage SHALL move unsent instructions to the fallback rail only after the partner confirms non-execution or the instruction ages into CNV-PAY-004 Unknown handling. The partner contract SHALL include a status-query API and segregated (FBO) holding. AC: a partner unreachable for 2 hours with instructions marked SentWithRequestId does not move those instructions to fallback; unsent ones move with the same idempotency chain.

claim: The per-donor exposure cap in CNV-FIN-003 counts 'all reversible un-matured amounts'. Unauthorized-return and warranty windows run up to two years, so nearly every ACH gift stays 'un-matured' for two years and active donors will hit the cap and have availability deferred.
why_it_matters: Regular donors will see unexplained availability delays, which drives service contacts and complaints. Exposure is overstated because warranty claims after 60 days are rare.
recommended_change: Define exposure as the sum, over return classes, of amount times a treasurer-approved risk weight, with weights decaying by age (for example 100% inside the unauthorized-return window and a small weight afterwards). AC: a donor whose only un-matured gifts are 70 to 700 days old does not trigger the cap at a configuration where the same amount at day 10 would.

claim: Death handling for recurring grants is ambiguous. Report 04 says recurring grants are suspended pending successor authority. TEV-005 suspends future occurrences only once succession starts. CNV-ENT-001 says approved unpaid grants proceed unless sponsor policy says otherwise. INV-13 revalidates each occurrence. None says whether future occurrences of a series count as 'approved unpaid grants'.
why_it_matters: Families will get inconsistent treatment, and grants may be paid against the deceased's wishes or wrongly stopped.
recommended_change: State explicitly: installments already approved and reserved proceed. Future occurrences of a series whose only authorizing advisor has died SHALL be suspended from the date of credible notice until a successor confirms, unless program terms say otherwise. AC: a sole advisor's death notice on 5 April suspends the 1 May occurrence, while the 1 April installment approved on 28 March still pays.

claim: The complaint definition in CNV-PLT-005 ('any expression of dissatisfaction, justified or not', acknowledged within 2 business days and escalated at day 15) has no triage rule separating complaints from inquiries and no evidence of workload at E4 volume. Its acceptance criteria test only clocks.
why_it_matters: Agents will over- or under-classify inconsistently, and complaint metrics become meaningless for regulators and sponsors.
recommended_change: Keep the definition, but add a deterministic classification rule set with examples, allow automatic acknowledgment, and measure complaint incidence in the CNV-EVB-001 time study before staffing. AC: a sample of 200 contacts double-coded by two agents reaches a sponsor-set agreement rate before activation.

claim: Several numbers that drive design or contracts lack a cited basis or are labelled inconsistently: UNB-XIN-EVA-013's '50% of benchmarked capacity', 'p99 outbox lag 60 s' and '3x Fidelity-scale year-end spike'; UNB-XIN-IAM-005's 4-hour break-glass expiry and 1-hour notice; CNV-ENT-002's 90-day and 35-day exit periods; CNV-GOV-007's 30-day window; and RR-UNB-RES-003-r1's RTO of 4 or 24 hours. Report 03 claims every invented number became a method or an illustrative label.
why_it_matters: Benchmarking against another organization's scale ('Fidelity-scale') does not reflect the declared workload. Contractual numbers without an owner cannot be defended.
recommended_change: Label each as a business-policy default with an owner, rationale and review date. Replace 'Fidelity-scale' with the declared largest-sponsor workload from the CNV-ARC-001 workload envelope. AC: the validator fails on any numeric literal in a normative clause that has no basis tag {authority, policy-default, measured, illustrative}.

claim: Several clauses are not testable as written: 'prompt exception review' (CNV-GOV-003); 'reasonable with cost-based evidence' (CNV-GRT-013); 'SHALL NOT make lawful transfer effectively impossible' (CNV-ENT-002); 'wording SHALL be validated by sponsor usability research' (CNV-GOV-005); and 'partner and program isolation SHALL be threat-tested' (CNV-ARC-002), which has no pass criterion.
why_it_matters: Untestable requirements cannot be evidenced for SOC control design or for acceptance.
recommended_change: Replace each with a measurable criterion. Exceptions are reviewed within N business days, set by the sponsor. Charges are reasonable when the recovery ratio is at most the review trigger, backed by the cost study. Exit fees are capped at the fully allocated cost of the transfer. Usability passes at a sponsor-set task-success rate with at least 5 participants per role. Threat testing passes with zero cross-partner rows in the defined negative suite.

claim: The December readiness gate tests only that a surge plan exists. Its acceptance criterion fails only when no plan is recorded, although the clause text and TEV-001 require that 'simulated peak SHALL meet each legal deadline'. The modelled attainment of about 0.70 against the internal target is not an acceptance condition anywhere.
why_it_matters: A paper plan passes the gate while statutory deadlines (contemporaneous acknowledgments, OFAC 10-business-day reports) are missed at peak.
recommended_change: Add acceptance criteria. The gate SHALL pass only when a simulation of P90 forecast December arrivals against the rostered capacity (including double absence) shows every legal deadline met and internal service attainment at or above the sponsor-approved floor. Otherwise the plan SHALL fail and the sponsor executive SHALL accept the risk explicitly. AC: a plan whose simulation misses the OFAC reporting deadline for 3% of cases fails the gate.
